clue.text: Feelings of anxiety linked to son's pet

parts.note: cares are worries or feelings of anxiety
S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A child's pet is causing worry in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to stroke them fondly, a verb synonym for a gentle loving touch.

clue.text: Constant among leaders of Young Conservatives on the way up is male sceptical attitude

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the preceding letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant in maths and physics, such as the speed of light
in is a synonym of among

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young Tory rising through the party has a cynical man's outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns C + IN + YC into CYNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynicism is a distrustful, sceptical outlook on people's motives.

clue.text: One's woolly memory?

explanation.surface: Someone's memory has gone fuzzy.
explanation.walkthrough: A male sheep is woolly; RAM is also a computer's random-access memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a woolly male sheep, and RAM is computer working memory.

clue.text: Take over genuine records, just one thousand, to augment volume

indicators.note: to take over is to turn something over, so the assembled letters are read backwards
just one thousand means only a single K is kept, dropping the other

parts.note: pukka is Anglo-Indian slang for genuine
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: Someone buys real records, a thousand of them, and turns the volume up.
explanation.walkthrough: PUKKA with only one K is PUKA; add EPS and 'Take over' reverses PUKAEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak up is to talk louder, increasing the volume of one's voice.

clue.text: Examination of concrete structure

explanation.surface: An engineer inspects a concrete building.
explanation.definitionFit: A physical is a medical check-up; physical also means material or bodily, having tangible structure rather than abstract form.

clue.text: Continuo player possibly playing choir its D sharp

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A choir sings its D sharp while the continuo accompanies.
explanation.walkthrough: Continuo is the bass accompaniment in Baroque music, often taken by a keyboard; 'possibly' marks this player as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpsichordist commonly plays the continuo part in Baroque ensembles, so is an example of such a player.

clue.text: Poet's basic structure lacking English

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is missing from the word before

parts.note: a skeleton is a basic framework or structure

explanation.surface: A poet's work has a bare outline but no English polish.
explanation.walkthrough: John Skelton was an English poet of the Tudor period.
explanation.definitionFit: John Skelton was a poet, tutor to the young Henry VIII.

clue.text: Attach ropes badly .. tragic event

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are tied together wrongly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ropes tied badly lead to a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a disaster, a tragic event; in drama it is the tragic climax.

clue.text: Extra shelter from weather needed around Great Britain by end of February

indicators.note: needed around means the shelter word is wrapped about the letters that follow

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other
end of points to the last letter of February

explanation.surface: Extra cover from the weather is needed across Britain at the end of February.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat; a LEG BYE is one, run after the ball hits the batsman's body.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg bye is a type of extra in cricket, a run credited to the team rather than the batsman.

clue.text: Fixes managing salesman over condescending manner

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier pieces sit above the later one

parts.note: running means managing, as in running a business
a rep is a sales representative
airs are affected, superior manners

explanation.surface: A salesman with a patronising attitude is put in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Running repairs are small fixes made as needed while something stays in use.

clue.text: Style of wartime genre — mud and gore turns out good when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters gathered here are strewn into a new order
turns out means ejects, so a letter is thrown out of the word gore

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a blood-and-guts war film genre as merely broadcast filler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' expels G (good) from GORE, leaving ORE; 'when broadcast' then scatters GENRE + MUD + ORE into the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A nom de guerre is literally a war name, a pseudonym; to style someone is to name them.

clue.text: This powerful boat is turning stomach

indicators.note: turning here means the word for stomach is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the gut is the stomach or belly

explanation.surface: A powerful boat on rough water makes one queasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful vessel used to tow larger ships, so it fits a description of a strong boat.

clue.text: Elegant chap in daring game

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
Ken is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A stylish fellow plays a risky game of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is a game of nerve where players dare each other until one backs down.

clue.text: "Caution, lion about!" This may help avoid rabies

indicators.note: about indicates the letters are turned about into a different order

explanation.surface: A warning sign about a lion, with advice on preventing rabies.
explanation.definitionFit: An inoculation is a vaccination, which can protect against diseases such as rabies.

clue.text: One day of the week is fairly empty to meet

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday
taken as written

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone finds one weekday fairly quiet for getting together.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a need or demand is to satisfy it, a standard synonym in requirements language.

clue.text: Go pinch present when taking a turn round here?

definitions.text: Go pinch present when taking a turn round here?

indicators.note: taking a turn round suggests the letters of the phrase spin into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to shoplift a gift while strolling round a mall.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of GO PINCH PRESENT rearrange, and the clue as a whole describes a place where one strolls around tempted to pilfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping centre is a place where you take a turn round the stores, perhaps tempted to pinch a gift.

clue.text: Lavish friend holding party up in costume

indicators.note: holding means the friend word contains the other letters

parts.note: pal means friend

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: rig is clothing or costume, as in a rig-out

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A generous friend hosts a fancy-dress party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lavish' is an adjective here, not a verb; 'up' turns the party word over before it goes into the costume word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully lavish, as in the prodigal son who spent freely.

clue.text: Full glass by full glass, a motorist can't drive easily in such a condition

definitions.text: a motorist can't drive easily in such a condition

parts.note: a bumper is a glass filled to the brim
by can mean to, as in face by face or face to face
a second brimming glass, again a bumper

explanation.surface: Glass after glass leaves a driver too drunk to drive easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drink-driving, but the condition meant is heavy, crawling traffic with cars nose to tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper-to-bumper describes congested traffic where vehicles are packed nose to tail and cannot move freely.

clue.text: Outlook's right for court to do well

indicators.note: right for court means R replaces CT, the abbreviations of right and court

parts.note: a prospect is an outlook or view of the future

explanation.surface: The forecast is right for a legal case to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or flourish, to do well in life or business.

clue.text: Try to attract attention from London-bound coach

explanation.surface: A passenger on a coach to London tries to grab the spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go 'up' to London; a stage is a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage is to draw attention away from someone; split as UP STAGE it is a coach going up to London.

clue.text: Answer pages allow limited application of computing

parts.note: let means allow

explanation.surface: Answer pages permit only limited use of computers.
explanation.definitionFit: An applet is a small, limited program that runs within another application.

clue.text: Dish found near front of a menu that's pretty impenetrable

definitions.text: Dish found near front of a menu

explanation.surface: A starter on the menu is thick enough to stand a spoon in.
explanation.walkthrough: Soup is a dish that sits near the start of a menu; a 'pea-souper' is also a fog so thick it can scarcely be seen through.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is a dish served as a starter and a London nickname for dense, impenetrable fog.

clue.text: Start to look pregnant? Girl's got to mind

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, here with its possessive s
to tend is to mind or look after

explanation.surface: A girl starts to show a pregnancy and must look after herself.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell outward, as a belly does in pregnancy; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Floral tribute-Hawaii gives it, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A garland of flowers is offered in Hawaii as a welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of Floral, tribute and Hawaii spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a garland of flowers given as a greeting in Hawaii, a floral tribute.

clue.text: Father concerned with placing bet is using great care

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
in can mean involved or concerned with, as in being in business
staking is putting money down as a wager

explanation.surface: A dad agonises over where to lay his bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Painstaking means extremely careful and thorough, taking pains over the details.

clue.text: Activity of criminals stealing five diamonds

indicators.note: stealing means the criminals' word has a letter taken away from it

parts.note: vice is criminal activity, as in a vice squad
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Criminals steal five diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their glittering, frozen look.

clue.text: Mystic character evident in Metropolitan Tristan

indicators.note: evident in says the answer can be seen sitting within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A mystical figure appears in an opera production of Tristan at the Met.
explanation.walkthrough: Tristan is a Wagner opera, and the Metropolitan is New York's opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrist is a follower of tantra, the esoteric mystical tradition of Hinduism and Buddhism.

clue.text: Significant outside pressure before East's revoke

indicators.note: outside means the first word wraps around the following letters

parts.note: real can mean significant or substantial, as in a real difference

indicators.note: before places one letter ahead of the next

parts.note: P is the scientific abbreviation for pressure
E is the abbreviation for East, as on a compass

explanation.surface: A bridge player under pressure from East revokes.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge 'revoke' means failing to follow suit, but here it is the plain verb meaning cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or annul it, a straight synonym from legislation.
